summary: The Methods give the reaction volumes for PCR and Golden Gate setup, and the missing cycling and transformation details can be filled with defensible defaults. But the paper never identifies the seven Level 1 constructs (which backbone, promoter, CDS and terminator) or the colony-PCR genotyping primers. Without those, the expected amplicons in Fig 1D can't be reproduced or judged, so the measured outcome would be invalidated.

gaps.detail: Identity and sequences of the colony-PCR genotyping primers (Fig 1D); the paper only says they come from the BOTany1 primer dilution, and the primer list is not in the text
gaps.why_needed: The primers define the amplicon sizes used to judge whether each of the seven assemblies is correct, and Fig 1D cannot be interpreted without them.

gaps.detail: Identity of the seven Plant MoClo Level 1 assemblies: which of the seven L1 acceptors (backbone), which promoter, which CDS for each construct, and which terminator (Fig 1C is not in the text)
gaps.why_needed: The parts determine what is assembled and the expected amplicon size. Using different parts would not reproduce the experiment.

gaps.detail: Concentrations or amounts of the Level 0 parts and L1 acceptor in the 1 µL aliquots used for Golden Gate
gaps.why_needed: The ligation and digestion efficiency depends on the insert:acceptor molar ratio.
gaps.resolution: Use about 100-200 ng of acceptor plasmid with a 2:1 insert:acceptor molar ratio (from the TSL Plant MoClo protocol). Normalise part stocks so that 1 µL delivers roughly this, or use about 20 fmol/µL (as in other MoClo protocols).

gaps.detail: Golden Gate thermocycling program (the paper says only that users set ligation time, temperature and cycle number in BOTany3 version A; Supplementary Method 3 is deferred)
gaps.why_needed: The digestion-ligation cycling determines assembly efficiency. The paper gives only the ligase temperatures of 22°C (Thermo) and 16°C (NEB).
gaps.resolution: Use the Plant MoClo long-protocol cycling from the TSL guide, with the ligase-appropriate low temperature (16°C for NEB T4, 22°C for Thermo T4 per the paper). The TSL program is 26 cycles of 37°C for 3 min and 16°C for 4 min, then 50°C for 5 min and 80°C for 5 min. The guide also lists a 20 s 37°C step and a 'x3' that I could not reliably map to either program. A reaction volume of 10 µL is used.

gaps.detail: Primer stock concentrations: s4.2 says '100mM' stocks and '10 mM' working primers, which are physically implausible
gaps.why_needed: The final primer concentration in the PCR depends on the stock concentration.
gaps.resolution: The main text states stocks are 100 µM, with 10 µM working stocks. Add water in µL equal to nmol x 10 to get 100 µM, which is about 250 µL for 25 nmol. 1 µL of 10 µM in 10 µL gives 1 µM final, at the top of the VWR range of 0.1-1 µM.

gaps.detail: Colony PCR thermocycling program (not given; deferred to Supplementary Method 2)
gaps.why_needed: Cycling is needed to amplify the expected products.
gaps.resolution: Use the VWR Red Taq three-step program: 95°C for 2 min; 25-35 cycles of 95°C for 20-30 s, annealing for 20-40 s at 3-5°C below primer Tm (50-65°C range), and 72°C for 30 s (about 1 min/kb); then 72°C for 5 min. For colony PCR, use 30-35 cycles and a longer initial denaturation of 5 min (standard practice) to lyse cells. The annealing temperature and extension time must be set from the (unknown) primers and amplicon sizes.

gaps.detail: Colony PCR template preparation: how many colonies per construct, how they are picked and resuspended, and which plates (blue/white screening)
gaps.why_needed: The template for the 1 µL DNA input comes from E. coli colonies.
gaps.resolution: Pick white colonies from the antibiotic plates (50 µg/mL carbenicillin, for L1). Use about 5 colonies per construct, as in Fig 3. Touch a tip to each colony, resuspend in 20-50 µL of water, and use 1 µL as template. Also restreak or patch the colony so it can be recovered.
gaps.source: standard practice; colony numbers per the main-text Fig 3 legend

gaps.detail: Heat-shock transformation parameters (BOTany4-Shock&Go, Supplementary Method S4): cell and DNA volumes, heat-shock temperature and time, recovery medium and volume
gaps.why_needed: These steps determine the colony yield from which colony PCR templates are taken.
gaps.resolution: The paper gives the following. Chemically competent TOP10F' cells made by the CaCl2/MgCl2 method (s4.4) are used. The on-deck thermocycler heat-shocks and cools the cells, then adds a nutrient-rich medium. Recovery lasts 1 h on-deck. Plating is 50 µL on 60 mm low-salt LB agar with 50 µg/mL carbenicillin, plus 10 µL X-gal (20 mg/mL) and 30 µL IPTG (100 mM). Plates are incubated overnight at 37°C. Assume: 5-10 µL of assembly into 25-50 µL of thawed cells; 20-30 min on ice; 42°C for about 45 s; 2 min on ice; then add 100-200 µL of SOC or LB at 37°C. The medium identity, volumes and heat-shock time are not in the paper.
gaps.source: s4.4 and main-text Results; the rest is standard practice

gaps.detail: Gel electrophoresis conditions to read the colony PCR products
gaps.why_needed: Needed to visualise the amplicons in Fig 1D.
gaps.resolution: Load 5-10 µL of the PCR directly, since Red Taq contains loading dye. Run on a 1% agarose gel with a DNA ladder and stain with a standard nucleic acid stain. The red dye front runs at about 1000-2000 bp on a 1% gel.

retrieved_details:
From the paper (s4.2, s4.3, main text): 10 µL colony-PCR reaction = 5 µL Red Taq 2X Master Mix (VWR 76620-474) + 2 µL water + 1 µL each primer (10 µM; the Methods text 'mM' is a typo) + 1 µL template. Primer stocks are 100 µM (from 25 nmol dry oligos, typically 100-300 µL water), diluted to 10 µM. Golden Gate reaction = 10 µL total: 4 x 1 µL parts (backbone, promoter, CDS, terminator) + 6 µL master mix (1 µL 10 mM ATP (Thermo R0441), 1 µL 10x FastDigest buffer, 0.5 µL FastDigest Eco31I (BsaI), 0.5 µL T4 ligase (Thermo EL0012 at 22°C, or NEB M0202 at 16°C), 3 µL water). Cold block set to about 14°C for enzymes. Kit: Plant MoClo (Addgene 1000000044); L1 selection is carbenicillin 50 µg/mL.

From the VWR Red Taq datasheet: reaction setup is 1x master mix, 0.2 µM each primer (0.1-1 µM range), and a 3-step program of 95°C for 2 min; 25-35 cycles of 95°C for 20-30 s, 50-65°C (about 3-5°C below Tm) for 20-40 s, and 72°C for 30 s (about 1 kb/min); then 72°C for 5 min. https://digitalassets.avantorsciences.com/adaptivemedia/rendition?id=85c86049b8ccf300533e94dc659666495a63abbe&vid=1b547798ce03127aff2f37f8ed165b2df99c4165&prid=original&clid=SAPDAM

From the TSL Plant MoClo guide: BsaI level 1 long protocol cycling is 26 cycles of 37°C for 3 min and 16°C for 4 min, then 50°C for 5 min and 80°C for 5 min. Use 100-200 ng of acceptor and a 2:1 molar ratio of insert:acceptor. https://synbio.tsl.ac.uk/uploads/a94d80d88a4d03acbe8b53da74fdcf49.pdf

From the paper's main text (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.08.21.671538v1.full.pdf): Level 1 vectors have a promoter, various CDS and a terminator, and seven assemblies were scored by colony PCR. The BOTany4 transformation uses on-deck heat shock, cooling, addition of recovery medium and a 1 h on-deck recovery. The paper does not give the part list, the primer sequences, or the cycling and heat-shock settings.
